I always advise anyone to wait for an MZ sale. As a lot of the sales are like 40-50% off or there round about it.  But MZ has a lot of QOL features over MV.
1. Multiple layers. So if you ever played RPG maker XP. you can choose which layer you can place tiles on.
2. Event tree tab. On maps, you can see an event tree, showing all the events on the map.
3. Changing the screen resolution. You can change the screen res of the game.
4. Set your own tileset sizes. You can choose the size of the tilesets you want to use in the maker.
This is just the top of my head, but if you can, download the demo and check out the features yourself as I think this would be the bets method in checking out the engine and it's features

posts.author: Andar

What is missing in the list above is the ability to use particle animations in addition to old-style animations (although the MV-compatible animations are a bit hidden, right-click on an empty animation name)
contrary to what is said above, MZ has exactly the same layers as MV - the difference is that you can switch between automatic and manual layer control where MV has only automatic layer control.
and there have been a lot of minor updates to many event commands

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
Andar said:
the only thing lost is the ability to port to Linux.
Click to expand...
This is technically not lost either – even though it doesn't explicitly have an export button for it, you could still manually make a Linux port. I don't even think it would be that difficult – download a Linux version of nwjs, copy over the www folder from your Windows build, and add a .desktop file (you could probably just copy the one from a Linux build of MV).
Alright, so let me see if I can make a more complete list of new features than other people have…
Mapping:
Quick Access panel – a panel that lets you add maps to it so you can view just a subset of the maps instead of your entire map hierarchy.
Event List panel – useful if you're trying to find an event by its name but don't remember exactly where it was on the map.
Show Passability option – overlays X's on impassable tiles; might be useful for parallax mappers. Unfortunately, it doesn't look like it shows 4-dir passability though.
Erase tool – you don't need to select specific "magic" tiles from the tile panel to erase anymore.
Manual layering – you can switch between MV's "automatic layering" or manual layering – picking the exact layer you place a tile on. This means A tiles can go on layers 3 and 4, and B-E tiles can go on layers 1 and 2, though there are good reasons
not
to put B-E tiles on layer 1, and A2
counter
tiles still only draw correctly when placed on layer 2.
Eventing:
There are new context menu options to insert a colour code or a text control character.
There's a new "Skip" option that lets you "comment out" a section of an event – you can select a bunch of commands and mark them as "skip", and they will literally be skipped over when the game runs.
Show Text now has a built-in name box.
Control Variables -> Game Data has a new "Last" option to get at the last skill or item used, or the last battler to act or be targeted.
Conditional Branch -> Button now lets you specify the state of the button – pressed, triggered, or repeated.
Scroll Map now has a "Wait for Completion" checkbox.
Set Movement Route now has a "Preview" button.
Show Balloon Icon now shows a preview of the chosen balloon, making it easier to use the user-defined balloons.
Show Picture and Move Picture now have a "Quick Setting" button that lets you visually specify the picture's position on the screen.
Move Picture how has an Easing option for non-linear speed curves.
Get Location Info now has a new "Designation by a character" option, allowing you to get the coordinates of the player or any event. (Note: you could already do this in MV via two Control Variables calls, but it's more convenient with Get Location Info.)
Plugin commands are edited like plugin parameters, rather than just being a single command string.
Database:
There's a new Attack Trait, "Attack Skill", which changes the skill used by the standard Attack command.
Item/Skill scope is now broken down into three parts and offers a few more options, like targeting both enemies and allies, or targeting both alive and dead characters.
Item, Skill, and State battle log messages are more flexible, no longer forcing you to put the user's or target's name first.
There's an entirely new animation system based on an external editor, Effekseer. You can still use the old system if you prefer.
You're now allowed to set A tiles to star passability in the tileset editor. 4-dir passability still isn't allowed (except for A5).  There's also a button to copy-paste tile settings from one tileset to another.
There's a lot more system settings – they've been divided into two tabs. The most notable new options are probably:
The Time Progress battle systems.
You can adjust Command Window position on the title screen.
You can also set the tile, icon, and face size to be smaller than the default (but not larger).
If 100 pictures isn't enough for you, you can increase the limit.
You can set the screen size to whatever you want.
Other:
There's a "Skip Title Screen" option in the Game menu
You can easily update (or downgrade) the core scripts in the Game menu.
There's a new "offset" function to fine-tune your faces in the Character Generator.
Deploy options adds an ignore list to specify files that shouldn't be copied.
Plugin manager is a bit easier to use, with an ON/OFF checkbox for each plugin and a clickable link the plugin details in many cases (provided by the plugin). For plugin developers, it also adds a few new data types. (Editing the parameters themselves hasn't been improved at all though.)
It's backwards-compatible with MV data, so if you don't use any plugins, it's trivial to port your MV project to MZ. (If you do use plugins, it depends on the plugins.)
That's still not a complete list, but it should give you a pretty good idea of what's changed, I think.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
You could say it's even better than that – if you find you don't like MZ after all, you could switch the project back to MV without too much trouble. The data's not 100% backwards-compatible, but it's pretty close. I think you'd have to fix all the skill, item, and state messages if you did that; I'm not aware of any other issues you'd find.
But in general I definitely recommend using MZ rather than MV. They're similar enough that the only reason to buy MV now (in my opinion) is the RTP.
From what I recall, all you need to do to port your game is to make a new project in MZ, then delete the data, img, audio, and js folders, and copy those folders (plus movies if you have any) over from your MV project. There might be a few other things you need to do (and I'd recommend using Update Corescript after you do that as well), but that's most of it, at least. You could also skip the js folder (and the corescript update) if you use absolutely no plugins at all; or if you use only a few plugins you could manually copy them over rather than deleting and copying the entire js folder.

posts.author: Piyan Glupak
posts.body:
A very minor factor for many, but in MV you can't set the A2 sheet overworld auto-tiles to '*' passibility without using a pair of plugins. You can do that in the editor with MZ. I like my parties to walk through the forest, not over it.
I prefer the default battle windows in MZ to MV, but MV seems a better bet if you want a battle-party larger than 4.
One minor nuisance with MZ is that when you start a new project, you have to deselect "Enable Autosave" in the editor unless you actually want it.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
Well, I checked earlier, and MZ offers three options for deployment – Windows, MacOS, and Mobile/Web.
But since MZ is built on web technology, it's literally just a website, so if you deploy for web and bundle the result with a Linux build of nwjs, you get a Linux build of your game. So, Linux is also fairly easy to do even without the explicit option.
